summary: AgniNet is a unified satellite fire intelligence platform that harmonizes MODIS and VIIRS active-fire observations using spatial and temporal matching. Powered by NASA FIRMS data, it provides interactive fire visualization, cross-sensor analysis, observation inspection, and historical fire analytics. AgniNet helps transform fragmented satellite observations into a unified view for clearer wildfire monitoring and data-driven analysis.
details:
AgniNet — Unified Satellite Fire Intelligence

1. Problem Statement

Wildfire monitoring relies on observations from multiple satellite systems, including MODIS and VIIRS. However, these observations may differ in spatial resolution, acquisition time, and detection characteristics. Analysing them separately can make it difficult to obtain a unified understanding of active-fire activity.

AgniNet addresses this challenge by bringing multi-satellite active-fire observations into a unified geospatial intelligence platform.

2. Our Solution

AgniNet is a satellite fire intelligence platform powered by NASA FIRMS data. It integrates MODIS and VIIRS observations, performs cross-sensor harmonization, and presents the results through an interactive dashboard.

The platform provides:

  • Global active-fire observation visualization.
  • Multi-sensor observation inspection.
  • Cross-sensor harmonization and classification.
  • Historical fire activity analytics.
  • Sensor comparison and regional fire analysis.
  • Satellite feed and operational status monitoring.

3. NASA FIRMS Integration

AgniNet integrates NASA Fire Information for Resource Management System (FIRMS) data to retrieve active-fire observations from multiple satellite feeds.

The platform processes MODIS and VIIRS observations, normalizes their attributes, and presents available satellite telemetry through a unified interface.

It supports multiple feeds, including MODIS NRT, VIIRS NOAA-20 NRT, VIIRS NOAA-21 NRT, and VIIRS SNPP NRT. Partial feed failures are handled so that available observations can still be presented.

4. MODIS–VIIRS Harmonization

The core innovation of AgniNet is its cross-sensor harmonization engine.

It uses spatial and temporal matching techniques, including Haversine distance calculations and footprint-aware analysis, to identify relationships between observations from different satellite sensors.

Observations are classified into four categories:

  • MATCHED — observations associated across sensors.
  • MODIS_ONLY — observations without a corresponding VIIRS match.
  • VIIRS_ONLY — observations without a corresponding MODIS match.
  • AMBIGUOUS — observations with uncertain or competing associations.

The system preserves sensor-specific measurements, including Fire Radiative Power (FRP), rather than incorrectly combining measurements from different sensors.

5. Historical Fire Analytics

AgniNet includes historical analytics for exploring fire activity over time. Users can examine trends, calendar-based activity, regional distributions, sensor statistics, and harmonized events.

The platform distinguishes between live NASA FIRMS observations, historical database records, and synthetic demonstration datasets to maintain data transparency.

6. Technology Stack

Frontend:

  • Next.js and React
  • TypeScript
  • Tailwind CSS
  • MapLibre GL JS
  • Recharts and Lucide

Backend:

  • Python
  • FastAPI
  • Pandas and NumPy
  • SQLite for historical data persistence in the current deployment configuration

Geospatial Processing:

  • Haversine distance calculations
  • Footprint-aware spatial matching
  • Spatial and temporal filtering
  • Cross-sensor observation classification

Data Source:

  • NASA FIRMS

7. Impact and Future Potential

AgniNet aims to make multi-satellite fire observations easier to explore, compare, and analyse through a unified interface.

By harmonizing observations while preserving their individual sensor characteristics, the platform supports clearer interpretation of satellite-derived active-fire information.

It can serve as a foundation for further research and development in geospatial intelligence, wildfire monitoring, and satellite data analysis.

AgniNet does not claim to confirm physical fires or replace ground-based verification. It provides intelligence based on satellite-observed thermal anomalies.

AgniNet — One Fire Map. Multiple Satellites. Unified Intelligence.
